title: Upper Deck Seat Track and Floor Panel Rework for High Density Cabin Reconfiguration
abstract: Rework of the upper deck seat tracks and the floor panels between them, giving a continuous drained interface under the galley and lavatory monuments and the fitting pitch that a nine-abreast premium layout needs.

sections.reason: Corrosion under the upper deck galleys and lavatories has now been through two design answers. The sealed track section stopped fluid reaching the fastener holes and the titanium attachment lug removed the galvanic couple, but one operator has recorded twenty-nine findings in twenty-six months on five aircraft and the pattern has moved again, this time to the floor panel edge where it meets the track flange. In parallel, three operators have asked for a track pitch that supports a denser premium layout, and none of them will fit new seats on a track they still have to open every heavy check. The two requests share the same physical interface, so answering them separately would mean opening the upper deck floor twice.
sections.description: The seat track flange is reworked to a continuous drained profile that carries fluid to the existing floor drain rather than trapping it at the panel edge, and the floor panels between the tracks are replaced by items with a moulded upstand at the track interface. The titanium attachment lug D5350006194262 introduced by the previous standard is retained and re-used, as are the tension bolts LN231128K9, so the beam drilling is untouched. The sealed track web ARD386097-40 is renewed in the wet bays and re-used elsewhere, and clevis pins LN666073-13 are renewed at every splice. A new aft intercostal sub-assembly D5350116635044 is added at the two monument positions where the denser layout puts a seat leg between the existing intercostals, and the upper floor structure stiffener IND983416-78 is replaced by a taller item. Tubular spacers EN187472K9 set the panel-to-track standoff. Work is from the cabin side in zones 242, 265, 971 and 973, with the monuments and the cargo restraint seat track cover at FIN 12DL removed. Detail is on drawings D53501208297 and D53501140817.
sections.effects: Estimated mass increase of 21 kg per aircraft on a full upper deck installation, symmetric about the centre line, with a centre-of-gravity shift below 0.03 per cent mean aerodynamic chord. No electrical load change from the structure itself, although the denser layout raises cabin equipment load elsewhere. The reworked track is not interchangeable with either earlier standard: the panel upstand and the track profile only mate with each other. The repeat corrosion inspection of the upper deck wet areas can be dropped once the whole deck is converted, but not before. Maintenance manual, illustrated parts and structure repair content for the upper deck floor all require update, and at least one published repair scheme sits in the area the new upstand occupies.
sections.embodiment_note: Retrofit only. Provisional estimate is nine days with the upper deck cabin already stripped for the reconfiguration, and sixteen days as a standalone task. Kits are ordered by bay. No production cut-in is proposed.
sections.open_points: Pre-analysis must establish whether the rework can be embodied on aircraft that never took the sealed track section standard, whether the published upper deck floor repair scheme survives the panel upstand, and whether the under-seat equipment boxes that another candidate proposes to relocate can still be mounted on the reworked track profile.

type_data.balance_impact: Symmetric installation, CG shift below 0.03 % MAC
